title: user_actions
description: A service declares the END-USER (self-service) operations it supports, in its own /internal/manifest, under a `user_actions` array. The platform APP panel (GET /api/v1/app/catalog) aggregates these across every service, filtered to the actions the CALLER's own capabilities allow — the user's app, exactly as `admin_actions` is the operator's panel. Same shape, same rules; the difference is only WHICH routes you declare here: a user's own self-service routes (their files, their profile, their subscription), never platform-operator routes. THE PANEL IS A MAP, NEVER THE AUTHORITY: `capability` is declared only so the app hides a control the caller could not use; the owning service re-checks it, and re-scopes to the caller's tenant/identity, on every call. Any service in any language that emits this shape appears in the user app automatically.

id.description: Stable, service-unique id, e.g. `files.upload`. The app keys on it.

label.description: Human text for the control. UNTRUSTED — the renderer MUST escape it (a third-party service's label is stored-XSS otherwise).

method.description: Allow-list only. Anything else is refused by safety:user-actions.

path.description: A RELATIVE path on the DECLARING service. No scheme, no host, no query. The aggregator always invokes it at that service's discovered address — a declaration cannot name an arbitrary URL (SSRF).

capability.description: The capability the OWNING ROUTE already enforces. Declared so the app filters what it shows; never a substitute for the server-side check and tenant/identity re-scoping.

params.description: Form fields. Become inputs in the app.

confirm.description: The renderer requires an explicit re-confirm before submitting. UX only.

danger.description: Destructive/irreversible for the user (e.g. delete my account). Rendered distinctly and implies confirm. UX only.

group.description: Optional section label for grouping actions in the app.
